correctness.rationale: Direct combinatorial choice gives \(Z_{n;i,j}=n!\binom ni\binom nj/(n-i-j)!\), with disjointness equivalent to zero composition. Vandermonde yields the vacancy distribution and a hypergeometric conditional first rank. The normalized binomial ratio is in [0,1] and tends to 1 for fixed vacancy s, giving Poisson(1) in total variation by dominated convergence; fixed-s hypergeometric mean (n-s)/2 and variance (n-s)(n+s)/(4(2n-1)), with central Stirling local approximation and variance tightness, give N(0,1/2) for rank difference over sqrt(n). Summable bound on vacancy mass gives independence by dominated mixture. All partial maps and zero compositions \(0\le n\le4\) were checked directly. Infinite conclusions use analytic proof, not experiment. The normalizing constant and Gaussian variance were independently reconstructed.

value.rationale: Zero products are intrinsic to the multiplication of the symmetric inverse monoid and govern its annihilation relation. The previously known scalar count does not say which factor ranks produce such products. The conditional law exhibits two mathematically distinct scales: a tight Poisson(1) number of unused rank positions and a sqrt(n)-scale Gaussian imbalance independent of those vacancies; both factor ranks concentrate at n/2 rather than their unconditional near-full-rank regime. This gives a natural asymptotic classification over every n and may be useful for studies of zero-product graphs. No artificial parameter slice or unsupported downstream theorem is claimed.
